Appearance:
Shri Sourabh Neema, learned counsel along with Shri Gop  Neema, learned counsel for the petitioners.

None appeared for respondents No.1 and 2.
 Shri Akshansh Mehra, learned counsel appears on behalf   Kumar Mehra, learned counsel for respondent No.3.
 ORDER 1.
Considered IA No.882/2025 which is an application for direction for refund of additional Court fees paid by the appellants.
2. It is submitted by the learned counsel for the appellants that the appeal is valued at Rs.15,00,000/-.
However inadvertently Court fees of Rs.60,000/- has been paid thereupon.
The Court fees payable in view of the Court Fees (Madhya Pradesh Amendment) Act, 2012 on the date of filing of the appeal was 2.5% which would have been Rs.37,500/-.
Thus, additional Court fees of Rs.22,500/- has been paid by the appellants which deserves to be refunded.

3. On due consideration of the fact that Court fees payable on the amount of enhancement claimed in the appeal was 2.5% which would be Rs.37,500/- whereas inadvertently Rs.60,000/- Court fees has been affixed, the application is allowed and the appellants are held entitled for refund of excess amount of Court NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-IND:3556 2 MA-1389-2015 fees of Rs.22,500/- paid by them in this appeal.
Registry is directed to issue the requisite certificate in favour of the appellants for refund of the excess Court fees.

4. With the consent of learned counsel for the parties the matter is finally heard.

5. This appeal under Section 173 (1) of the Motor Vehicle Act, 1973 has been preferred by the appellants/claimants being aggrieved by the award dated 01.05.2015 passed in MACC No.20/2015 by the 7th Additional Member, Motor Accidents Claims Tribunal, Indore whereby a total sum of Rs.16,80,000/- has been awarded to them by way of compensation.

6. The facts of the case in brief are that on 17.05.2012, at about 11.00 a.m., Jagdish Patidar, husband of appellant No.1, father of appellants 2, 3 and 6 and son of appellants 4 and 5, was going on his motorcycle to Dwarikapuri.

At that time a dumper bearing registration No.MP-09-GS-4514 which was being driven by respondent No.2 and was owned by respondent No.1 and was insured with respondent No.3 dashed against his motorcycle as a result of which he fell down and suffered grievous injuries.
He was taken to the hospital for treatment but eventually expired.
7. Thereafter the appellants filed an application under Section 166, 140 of the Act, 1988 for award of compensation to them on account of death of Jagdish Patidar.
The application was contested by respondent No.3 by filing its written statement to the same.
After evaluation of the evidence brought on record by the parties the Claims Tribunal has awarded compensation to the appellants as aforesaid.

8. This appeal for enhancement of amount of compensation has been preferred by the appellants on the ground that the Claims Tribunal has not taken NEUTRAL CITATION NO.
2025:MPHC-IND:3556 3 MA-1389-2015 any note of the fact as regards the future prospects of rise in income of the deceased.
At the time of the accident, he was aged about 28 years.
He would have hence worked for a number of years in which his income would have risen at a steady pace.
It has been held by the Apex Court in a number of cases that while determining the award of compensation, future prospects have to be necessarily taken into consideration.
The amount awarded under the head of loss of consortium is also grossly inadequate.
It is hence submitted that the amount awarded to the appellants be enhanced appropriately.

9. Per contra, learned counsel for respondent No.3 Insurance Company has submitted that just and proper amount of compensation has been awarded to the appellants in which no interference is warranted in view of which the appeal deserves to be dismissed.
10. I have considered the submissions of the learned counsel for the parties and have perused the record.
11. The accident in question took place in the year 2011.
The deceased was aged about 28 years at that time.
He was in occupation as a Traffic Assistant and Part Time Meter Mechanic.
There would have certainly been a steady rise in his income for a number of years.
The same has not at all been taken into consideration by the Claims Tribunal.
It has been well settled by the Apex Court in a series of decisions that future prospects of rise in income are bound to be taken note of.
Considering the age of the deceased the same deserve to be taken at 40%.

2 12.
The yearly income of the deceased which has been taken at Rs.1,20,000/- per year is liable to be increased by 40% for future prospects of rise in income which would be Rs.48,000/-.
The total income would hence be Rs.1,68,000/- per year.

Deducting 1/4th for personal expenses i.e.
Rs.42,000/- the NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-IND:3556 4 MA-1389-2015 annual loss of dependency would be Rs.1,26,000/- per year.
The multiplier of 17 applied by the Claims Tribunal is appropriate.
The total amount for loss of dependency is hence worked out Rs.21,42,000/-.
13. It is further observed that the appellants are six in number.
They are all entitled for award of compensation to them in the shape of loss of consortium.
The same looking to the age of the deceased deserves to be taken at Rs.48,000/- per claimant i.e. Rs.2,88,000/- in all.
The amount awarded for funeral expenses and loss of estate is just and proper.

14. Thus the appellants are held entitled for award of total sum of Rs.24,66,000/- to them by way of compensation whereas the Claims Tribunal has erred in awarding them a sum of Rs.16,80,000/-
only.

The appellants are hence entitled for award of enhanced amount of Rs.7,86,000/- to them by way of compensation which shall be payable to them along with interest @ 6% per annum from the date of filing of the claim application till date of payment.
15. The appeal is accordingly partly allowed and disposed off.
